newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso pares slide as speculation eases.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso pares slide as speculation eases.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed softer for the first time in eight sessions on Monday, but moderated earlier falls as light speculation subsided, dealers said.
"Dollars were in demand earlier from foreign investors; then a big corporate player jumped in to sell at the close," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended trade 0.2 and 0.3 of a centavo weaker, respectively, at 7.8545/7.8590 and 7.8530/7.8560 per dollar.
"After that, other players who were long on dollars followed suit," the trader added.
Dealers said the market awaited the outcome of Tuesday evening's central bank auction of government securities.
"If demand for paper is low at the auction, foreign investors may not like it," another trader said.
Same-day peso contracts had closed earlier 1.65 centavos weaker at 7.8545/7.8590 per dollar.
